text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals group Roche Holding AG said Thursday its 1996 sales rose 11 percent to 15.96 billion Swiss francs ($11.6 billion) and profits were again expected to rise.
Roche, the second-largest Swiss pharmaceuticals firm, said a significant gain in volume sales helped it boost its position in key markets and sectors despite downward pressure on prices.

Sales of Roche's leading products, such as Rocephin -- the world's top-selling injectable antibiotic -- continued to grow and new products, such as the AIDS drug Invirase, were very well-received by the market.
Roche said its operating results had strengthened on the back of higher capacity utilization in its factories and steady gains in efficiency.
"Taking into account another good result for the group's non-operating activities as well, Roche expects to see consolidated net income increase once again," it said in a statement.
Roche's profit forecast is similar to a previous forecast made in October, when it said that 1996 profits would exceed 1995's group net profit of 3.37 billion Swiss francs ($2.46 billion).

Higher drugs sales were achieved not only in North America and Europe -- the two most important markets -- but also in Brazil, Mexico, Australia and other major markets. Solid volume growth in Japan helped offset a decline in revenue from government-mandated price cuts.
